classification_signals: Abstract explicitly states: 'We therefore review relevant literature to explore the potential for place attachment...'
Introduction states: 'The work here situates the concept of place attachment within green building discourse.'
The paper synthesizes existing research to propose theoretical connections and future research directions, rather than presenting new empirical data.
Section headers like 'Future research directions' (p. 3, 4, 6) indicate a review and conceptual development focus.
The paper includes conceptual diagrams (Fig. 1, Fig. 2) illustrating proposed relationships.
title: Place attachment in green buildings: Making the connections

limitations: The current theoretical framework lacks explicit directionality in the relationships between constructs, requiring future quantitative and qualitative research to explore causality and interrelations (p. 6).
There is a deficit of empirical work on place attachment in green buildings, necessitating extensive future research across diverse populations and building types (p. 7).

The attitudes and knowledge of building occupants are key moderators for place attachment processes in green buildings, particularly how environmental identity intersects with green building context (p. 7).

The 'visible environmentalism' of a building is subjective, depending on individual perception and knowledge, rather than being an objective quality, which complicates its role in place identity (p. 7).
Place attachment processes in green buildings may be confounded with 'workplace attachment', which focuses on the socio-cultural work environment and connection to it (p. 7).
Other spatial scales (adjacent buildings, neighborhoods, urban centers, natural areas) may interrelate with building attachment and should be measured or controlled for in future research (p. 7).
minimum_safe_summary: This narrative review explores the potential for place attachment to develop in green buildings, proposing theoretical connections between green design strategies and psychological processes of place attachment (affect, identity, and dependence). Key findings suggest that biophilic design, visible environmentalism, support for pro-environmental behaviors, and good indoor environmental quality can foster place attachment, which in turn may enhance occupant wellbeing and pro-environmental behaviors. However, the paper highlights a significant deficit of empirical research in this area, noting that individual and cultural differences, as well as confounding factors like workplace attachment and broader spatial scales, need to be addressed in future studies to establish causality and specific relationships.

theory_commitments.specific_claim: The paper extends existing conceptualizations of place attachment to the context of green buildings, exploring how specific design strategies foster its affective, identity, and dependence dimensions.
The paper assumes the innate human tendency to connect with nature, proposing that biophilic features in green buildings facilitate this connection, contributing to place attachment.

The paper proposes that the physical characteristics and design strategies of green buildings significantly influence human psychological states, behaviors, and ultimately, the formation of place attachment.

mechanism_chain.description: The paper proposes that various green building design strategies foster place attachment by influencing users' perceptions of naturalness, promoting shared environmental values, supporting pro-environmental behaviors, and enhancing physical comfort, which collectively contribute to affective, identity, and dependence dimensions of attachment.
